title: Supervised, unsupervised or reinforcement?
description: Sort each Cairnway ML problem by how the model learns: from labeled examples, from unlabeled data, or from rewards.

items.text: Predict how many days late an order will arrive, from past orders whose delays are known.
items.why: Every past order comes with the answer (its actual delay), so the model learns from labeled examples. Predicting a number is regression.

items.text: Group customers into segments by buying habits, with no segments defined in advance.
items.why: Nobody labels the groups; the model finds structure by itself. This is clustering.

items.text: A warehouse robot learns the fastest picking route, getting a reward for each quick pick.
items.why: The robot learns by trial and error from rewards and penalties, not from labeled examples.

items.text: Classify product reviews as spam or not spam, from 10,000 reviews that staff already marked.
items.why: The marked reviews are labels. Predicting a category is classification.

items.text: Spot unusual card transactions when there are no examples marked as fraud.
items.why: Without labels, the model learns what normal looks like and flags what doesn't fit: anomaly detection.

items.text: Tell tents from backpacks in photos, after training on photos tagged with their category.
items.why: Each training photo carries its correct category, so this is supervised image classification.

items.text: Find products that are often bought together, from raw order baskets.
items.why: The baskets have no labels; the model discovers patterns in them (association).

items.text: An agent learns how much to bid for ads by trying bids and being rewarded for each sale that follows.
items.why: It improves its decisions over time from a reward signal, which is reinforcement learning.

items.text: Estimate a product's return rate from past products whose return rates are recorded.
items.why: The recorded return rates are labels, and the target is a number, so this is supervised regression.

items.text: Discover a customer segment nobody had named, such as 'weekend trail-runners', in purchase history.
items.why: The segment emerges from the data without labels: clustering.

items.text: A scheduling agent picks each day's delivery order, gets a reward when deliveries arrive on time, and improves its choices over time.
items.why: It learns by acting and receiving a score as reward, not from a fixed set of labeled answers.

items.text: Predict whether a customer will cancel their membership, from past members marked as stayed or left.
items.why: Past members are labeled with the outcome, so the model learns a yes/no classification from examples.
